title: Introduction
text: Seurat v5, new Assay type introduced called Assay5. Users can switch using Assay Assay5 classes store counts data setting global option Seurat.object.assay.version either “v3” “v5”. Similarly, pixelatorR, can set global option control whether use CellGraphAssay/PNAAssay CellGraphAssay5/PNAAssay5 class. CellGraphAssay/PNAAssay classes extend Assay class CellGraphAssay5/PNAAssay5 class extend Assay5 class, providing additional slots store spatial metrics component graphs.

title: Load data
text: Perhaps useful function ReadMPX_Seurat allows us load MPX data Seurat object additional bells whistles provided pixelatorR. , options modify Seurat created. First foremost, can set return_cellgraphassay = FALSE return Seurat object includes abundance measurements. simpler data set, count matrix stored Assay without spatial data. means almost information unique MPX ignored able analyze visualize graphs way explore spatial statistics. However, basic data set uses significantly less memory faster process can useful protein abundance interesting data type analysis. default, ReadMPX_Seurat returns MPX data object called CellGraphAssay. object class extends Assay class Seurat essentially Assay object additional data slots. CellGraphAssay class covered detail later tutorial. additional parameters ReadMPX_Seurat controls behavior return_cellgraphassay = TRUE. default, MPX polarization scores colocalization scores loaded stored CellGraphAssay named “mpxCells”.

title: Load data
text: edge list represents raw MPX data row corresponds edge formed UPIA UPIB pixel. information rarely needed analysis, required want load explore component graphs. ReadMPX_Seurat doesn’t load edge list memory, instead keeps track paths PXL file(s) associated data. can get path PXL file FSMap function: FSMap returns tibble paths PXL files associated Seurat object. case, one PXL file. “id_map” column list, element consists tibble component IDs can used look table map “current” component IDs “original” component IDs. unnest “id_map” column, can see current original component IDs: rename component IDs Seurat object, “current_id” column updated, “original_id” column remain unchanged: current IDs always unique, original IDs often duplicated components follow naming convention across data sets. table helps us map current IDs correct original IDs PXL file(s). need load MPX component graphs memory, can use LoadCellGraphs function. hood, LoadCellGraphs uses table sort edge list data stored, reads edge list data converts graph object per component. example, can load graphs two selected components like : can fetch loaded CellGraph objects two components using: NOTE: PXL file path invalid, e.g. file missing moved, LoadCellGraphs throw error.

Missing observations now set 0. Added option lazy ProximityScoresToAssay (PNAAssay Seurat methods) enable lazy evaluation proximity scores.

title: Changelog
text: layout_with_coarsened_pmds layout method faster accurate PNA cell graph layouts. ComputeProximityScores methods compute global proximity scores cell graphs. method also enables computing proximity scores k > 1 neighborhoods (lower spatial resolution), option limited log2 ratios (Z scores). heuristic_illumination approximate natural illumination 3D layout. Illumination masking option render_rotating_layout modulate node_val colors heuristic illumination mask. Shadow palette blending render_rotating_layout via illumination_shadow_colors palette-based shadow interpolation. normalize_illumination argument render_rotating_layout optionally disable rescaling illumination mask [0, 1]. “NaturalBlue” option gradient palette PixelgenGradient use natural illuminated color gradient.

title: Compute approximate edge saturation — approximate_edge_saturation
text: Edge saturation calculated : $$S_{edge} = 1 - \frac{E}{R}$$ \(E\) number unique edges \(R\) total read count. Higher saturation values indicate additional sequencing reads unlikely reveal new edges, suggesting sample sequenced near-saturation.

text: tibble following columns: component component (cell) identifier. read_count estimated number reads downsampling. p downsampling fraction. nodes estimated number nodes retained. edges estimated number edges retained. degree estimated average node degree. node_saturation node saturation given fraction. edge_saturation edge saturation given fraction.

title: Compute approximate saturation curve — approximate_saturation_curve
text: downsampling performed probabilistically using expected values rather actual random sampling. edge given read_count, probability edge retained fraction p : $$P(\text{edge retained}) = 1 - (1 - p)^{\text{read\_count}}$$ nodes, probability retention depends node's degree. node retained least one incident edges retained: $$P(\text{node retained}) = 1 - (1 - p_{edges})^{\text{degree}}$$ \(p_{edges}\) fraction edges retained.

title: Compute approximate saturation curve — approximate_saturation_curve
text: saturation values calculated using: $$S = 1 - \frac{N_{downsampled}}{R_{downsampled}}$$ \(N_{downsampled}\) number nodes edges downsampled graph, \(R_{downsampled}\) number reads supporting elements. Since read supports two nodes (one endpoint), \(R_{downsampled, nodes} = 2 \times R_{downsampled, edges}\).

title: Compute approximate saturation curve — approximate_saturation_curve
text: function requires approximate_node_saturation called first (either directly function) create nodes temporary view DuckDB connection.

title: Calculate dispersion of components — CalculateDispersion
text: Calculate dispersion numeric data Seurat object matrix. dispersion calculated summary statistic distribution values (counts) across components. dispersion can calculated using Gini coefficient Tau statistic. Gini Tau coefficients measures inequality distribution, ranging 0 1, 0 signifies perfectly equal distribution 1 signifies perfectly unequal distribution. terms marker counts across different markers component, low dispersion indicates marker counts similar levels across markers, high dispersion indicates marker counts distributed mostly one markers. dispersion can example used quantitative metric assess whether component's counts dispersed markers expected level. high low dispersion can indicate component kind artifact, rather real cell.

A tibble: 45 × 4 #>    marker_1 marker_2 estimate      p_adj #>    <chr>    <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> #>  1 M2       M1        -0.560  0.176      #>  2 M2       M10       -0.230  0.00639    #>  3 M3       M1         1.56   0.00858    #>  4 M3       M2         0.0705 0.0000275  #>  5 M3       M10        0.129  0.00147    #>  6 M4       M1         1.72   0.000311   #>  7 M4       M2         0.461  0.00114    #>  8 M4       M3        -1.27   0.00122    #>  9 M4       M10       -0.687  0.00000183 #> 10 M5       M1        -0.446  0.00283    #> # ℹ 35 more rows  # Typical heatmap ColocalizationHeatmap(dca_markers)   # Skip symmetrisation ColocalizationHeatmap(dca_markers, symmetrise = FALSE)   # Typical dot plot # Note that the size legend title needs to be set manually ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers,   type = "dots",   size_range = c(1, 10),   size_col_transform = \(x) {     -log10(x)   } ) &   labs(size = "-log10p(p_adj)")   # We can specify the order of the markers with factor levels # but we need to turn off the clustering ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers %>%     mutate(       marker_1 = factor(marker_1, levels = paste0("M", 1:10)),       marker_2 = factor(marker_2, levels = paste0("M", 1:10))     ),   type = "dots",   size_range = c(1, 10),   size_col_transform = \(x) {     -log10(x)   },   cluster_rows = FALSE,   cluster_cols = FALSE ) &   labs(size = "-log10p(p_adj)")   # ℹ 80 more rows  # This will now fail if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ColocalizationHeatmap(dca_markers_two_tests) } # }  # We need to subset the data first ColocalizationHeatmap(   dca_markers_two_tests %>%     filter(target == "stim1") )

title: Convert colocalization score table to an Assay or Assay5 — ColocalizationScoresToAssay
text: Takes object colocalization scores long format returns object colocalization scores wide format. colocalization score table includes various colocalization scores along p-values pair markers component. wide format array-like object dimensions (markers_1 * marker_2) x components, cell filled polarization score. Scores missing colocalization score table replaced 0's. Different outputs returned depending input object type: tibble/data.frame: returns matrix marker pairs rows components columns CelGraphAssay: returns Assay marker pairs rows components columns Seurat object: returns Seurat object new Assay marker pairs rows components columns many functions provided Seurat works Assay objects, sometimes convenient make conversion. instance, want compute UMAP colocalization scores RunUMAP, need values formatted Assay. also makes possible use various visualization functions VlnPlot FeaturePlor show distribution colocalization scores.

title: Compute proximity scores — ComputeProximityScores
text: expected mean calculated \(p_{umi1,m1} * p_{umi2,m2} * S0\), \(p_{umi1,m1}\) \(p_{umi2,m2}\)  frequencies two markers graph umi1 umi2 nodes, respectively. \(S0\) total number edges graph. formula variance join count statistic given (eq. 8, Epperson, B. K. 2002): $$ Var_{m1m2} = \frac{1}{4} \times (2S1p_{umi1,m1}p_{umi2,m2} + (S2 - 2S1)(p_{umi1,m1}p_{umi2,m2}(p_{umi1,m1} + p_{umi2,m2})) + 4(S1 - S2)(p_{umi1,m1}^2p_{umi2,m2}^2)) $$ $$ S1 = \frac{1}{2} \times (\sum_{,j} (A_{ij} + A_{ji})^2) $$ $$ S2 = \sum_{} \left(\sum_{j} (A_{ij} + A_{ji})^2\right) $$

title: Calculate edge weights for pMDS — edge_weights_for_pmds
text: Weights calculated edges graph bidirectional transition probability random walker. undirected edge \(e_{,j}\), define bidirectional transition probability \(P(e_{u,v}\) probability transitioning \(u\) \(v\) back \(u\) \(k\) steps. Note matter node random walker starts since go directions. computation, also allow self-loops graph slow transition random walker. , assume relationship bidirectional transition probability exponential function decays distance: $$P(e_{u,v}) \propto e^{-d(u, v)}$$ solving \(d(u, v)\), can define edge weight proportional distance: $$w_{u,v} = -\log(P(e_{u,v}))$$

title: Compute heuristic illumination for 3D layouts — heuristic_illumination
code: library(dplyr) set.seed(1)  # Here we simulate some 3D coordinates with a roughly spherical distribution n <- 20000 n_surface <- 19000 n_interior <- 1000  # Surface points: normalize to unit sphere, add small Gaussian noise xyz_surface <- matrix(rnorm(n_surface * 3), ncol = 3) xyz_surface <- xyz_surface / sqrt(rowSums(xyz_surface^2)) # project to unit sphere xyz_surface <- xyz_surface + matrix(rnorm(n_surface * 3, sd = 0.05), ncol = 3)  # Interior points: uniform in ball via rejection sampling xyz_interior <- matrix(rnorm(n_interior * 3), ncol = 3) radii <- runif(n_interior)^(1 / 3) # cube root for uniform volume distribution xyz_interior <- xyz_interior / sqrt(rowSums(xyz_interior^2)) * radii * 0.8  layout <- tibble::tibble(   x = c(xyz_surface[, 1], xyz_interior[, 1]),   y = c(xyz_surface[, 2], xyz_interior[, 2]),   z = c(xyz_surface[, 3], xyz_interior[, 3]) ) illum <- heuristic_illumination(layout)  # Create a temporary GIF file and render a rotating layout # using the computed illumination as node values temp_gif <- fs::file_temp(ext = ".gif") render_rotating_layout(   data = layout %>%     mutate(node_val = illum),   pt_size = 0.8,   width = 740,   height = 650,   colors = PixelgenGradient(100, "NaturalBlue"),   file = temp_gif,   max_degree = 30,   frames = 20,   delay = 1 / 20,   res = 100,   boomerang = TRUE,   show_first_frame = FALSE ) #> ! title: Compute LCC curve for downsampled edgelists — lcc_curve
text: LCC (largest connected component) measures graph connectivity. downsampling sequencing reads, edges removed probabilistically, eventually causes graph fragment smaller disconnected components. computing LCC sizes multiple downsampling fractions, can observe graph connectivity degrades reduced sequencing depth. Typically, sharp transition point LCC collapses, indicating minimum sequencing depth required maintain graph structure.

title: Compute LCC curve for downsampled edgelists — lcc_curve
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) pxl_file <- minimal_pna_pxl_file() components <- ReadPNA_counts(pxl_file) %>% colnames()  # Select fractions based on average read depth db <- PixelDB$new(pxl_file) avg_reads <- db$cell_meta()$reads %>% mean() fracs <- (10^seq(4, log10(avg_reads), length.out = 20))[-20] / avg_reads  lcc_df <- lcc_curve(pxl_file, components, fracs = fracs)  # Plot LCC sizes by fraction ggplot(lcc_df, aes(frac, n_nodes, color = component)) +   geom_point() +   geom_line() +   theme_bw() +   guides(color = "none")  # Compute graph stability (LCC / max theoretical nodes) nodesat <- approximate_node_saturation(db) %>% collect() db$close()  lcc_df <- lcc_df %>%   left_join(nodesat, by = "component")  ggplot(lcc_df, aes(frac, n_nodes / nodes, color = component)) +   geom_point() +   geom_line() +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +   labs(y = "Graph stability (LCC / total nodes)") +   theme_bw() +   guides(color = "none") } # }

Patch-specific means markers high abundant patch low abundant receiver cell. Optimal patch markers high abundant highly specific. method sensitive choice patch markers therefore requires careful selection. See identify_markers_for_patch_analysis information select patch markers. Patch detection can used find multiple patches single PNA graph. subgraphs can leveraged study patch protein composition, patch proximity scores, number patches fraction receiver cell covered patches. Note patches can appear cell debris artificial bleedover necessarily indicate cell-cell interaction. aim study patch composition response specific treatment condition, recommended include control population reference. Two algorithms available patch detection, described sections .

title: Simulate Sequencing Saturation Curve — SequenceSaturationCurve
text: function simulates effect lower read depth sequencing saturation PNA sample. can used create saturation curve given sample. function iteratively downsamples edgelist small number components records number edges, proteins, reads. saturation graph calculated step.

title: Simulate Sequencing Saturation Curve — SequenceSaturationCurve
code: SequenceSaturationCurve(   edgelist,   sample_fracs = rev(seq(0.1, 1, 0.1)),   n_comps = 10L )

title: Simulate Sequencing Saturation Curve — SequenceSaturationCurve
text: edgelist tibble containing edgelist following columns: component: component number. umi1: UMI first node umi2: UMI second node. read_count: number reads supporting edge. sample_fracs vector sample fractions downsample edgelist. resulting sizes exact, since parts graph may disconnected upon downsampling. function keep largest connected component. n_comps number components sample edgelist.

title: Simulate Sequencing Saturation Curve — SequenceSaturationCurve
text: tibble following columns: sample_size: number reads downsampled edgelist. sample_frac: fraction reads downsampled edgelist. graph_edges: number edges downsampled graph. graph_proteins: number proteins downsampled graph. graph_reads: number reads downsampled graph. graph_node_saturation: sequencing saturation graph based number proteins. graph_edge_saturation: sequencing saturation graph based number edges.

title: Simulate Sequencing Saturation Curve — SequenceSaturationCurve
code: library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) # Here we are reformatting an MPX edgelist to match the expected input # for a PNA edgelist  # Load the edgelist, and rename to match PNA input edgelist <-   ReadMPX_edgelist(system.file("extdata/five_cells", "five_cells.pxl",     package = "pixelatorR"   )) %>%   rename(umi1 = upia, umi2 = upib, read_count = count)  set.seed(37) seqsat <- SequenceSaturationCurve(edgelist,   sample_fracs = c(1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25),   n_comps = 2L )  # Calculate the mean sequencing saturation for each sample fraction seqsat_mean <-   seqsat %>%   group_by(sample_frac) %>%   summarise(     mean_node_saturation = mean(graph_node_saturation),     mean_edge_saturation = mean(graph_edge_saturation)   )  ggplot(seqsat_mean, aes(x = sample_frac, y = mean_node_saturation)) +   geom_line() +   labs(     title = "Sequencing Saturation Curve",     x = "Sample Fraction",     y = "Node Saturation (%)"   ) +   theme_minimal()   ggplot(seqsat_mean, aes(x = sample_frac, y = mean_edge_saturation)) +   geom_line() +   labs(     title = "Sequencing Saturation Curve",     x = "Sample Fraction",     y = "Node Saturation (%)"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Calculate Sequencing Saturation — sequencing_saturation
text: sequencing saturation calculated using formula: $$S = 100 \times \left(1 - \frac{E}{R}\right)$$ : \(S\) saturation (percentage), \(E\) number unique reads graph elements (e.g., nodes, edges), \(R\) number reads supporting elements graph. function can used calculating saturation : Reads: Number deduplicated reads vs. reads Nodes: Number nodes vs. reads Edges: Number edges vs. reads graph elements: Adjust input accordingly

text: asked generate test file function foo: Read source code R/ understand: function parameters types/defaults validation/assertions performs inputs returns (class, structure) Whether S4 methods multiple classes Identify correct test data (example, Seurat vs raw table). Write test file following three-part structure: Setup (data loading, outside test_that) Expected-behavior tests (data-level comparisons) Invalid-input tests (one per parameter feasible) Run tests confirm pass:
code: Rscript -e 'testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-foo.R")'

title: Skill: Generate Unit Tests for pixelatorR
text: full example ColocalizationHeatmap:
code: library(dplyr) prox <- ReadPNA_proximity(minimal_pna_pxl_file()) prox_summarized <- prox %>%   slice_sample(n = 1e4) %>%   group_by(marker_1, marker_2) %>%   summarize(mean_log2_ratio = mean(log2_ratio), .groups = "drop") %>%   mutate(test1 = marker_1, test2 = marker_2, estimate = mean_log2_ratio) %>%   ungroup()  test_that("ColocalizationHeatmap works as expected", {   # Default method   expect_no_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized))    # Dots method   expect_no_error(p <- ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, type = "dots",                                               size_col = "mean_log2_ratio"))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_1))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_2))   expect_equal(p$data$marker_1 %>% levels(), p$data$marker_2 %>% levels())    # Custom marker columns   expect_no_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized,                                          marker1_col = "test1",                                          marker2_col = "test2"))    # Custom value column   expect_no_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized,                                          value_col = "mean_log2_ratio"))    # Symmetrise FALSE   expect_no_error(p <- ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, symmetrise = FALSE,                                               type = "dots",                                               size_col = "mean_log2_ratio"))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_1))   expect_true(is.factor(p$data$marker_2))   expect_true(!identical(p$data$marker_1 %>% levels(),                          p$data$marker_2 %>% levels())) })  test_that("ColocalizationHeatmap fails with invalid input", {   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap("Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, marker1_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, marker2_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, value_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, type = "dots",                                       size_col = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized,                                       size_col_transform = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, size_range = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, colors = FALSE))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, cluster_rows = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, cluster_cols = "Invalid"))   expect_error(ColocalizationHeatmap(prox_summarized, type = "Invalid")) })
